RSP/functionalRequirements/FRE-REQU-LST-.description:
The system shall run an installation as a reserved platform
tenant plus customer tenants.
- Platform administrators are users of the platform tenant
  holding scoped platform rights, and delegation, four-eyes
  and audit apply to them unchanged.
- A tenant is in exactly one of the states provisioning,
  active, suspended or deleted.
- Creating a tenant requires its first top-level
  administrator, and a second one when the four-eyes principle
  is enabled for the tenant, unless the first is to approve as
  his own second (self-approval, D-306).
- The first administrator is invited by e-mail with a
  time-limited link to set a password and enrol a second
  factor.
- Platform administrators delete a tenant with four-eyes; a
  deleted tenant stays restorable for 90 days, then follows
  its own pseudonymization and purge rules, and a final data
  export is offered.

It shall also:
- create a tenant in state provisioning with its slug, display name,
  available features, four-eyes choice — on unless switched off — and
  self-approval setting, refusing a slug that is used or reserved
  (D-306);
- open the tenant (provisioning to active) once its first top-level
  administrator — both of them under four-eyes — has accepted the
  invitation;
- let platform administrators delete a tenant still in provisioning whose
  administrators never accepted, revoking its pending invitations;
- list the installation's tenants with slug, display name and state to
  platform administrators, without tenant data;
- let Tom SQM create a tenant when a customer makes its first subscription — through an operation of the administration API, called with the platform tenant's service account for Tom SQM — with the customer's subscriptions bound to it from the start and the person whose address the customer gave during the subscription for the first administrator — by default the person subscribing — invited as its first top-level administrator where those subscriptions include Tom UAM's administration, otherwise as its first inviter (BQ-398); every tenant is bound by the subscriptions of its customer;
- offer self-service tenants — tenants whose subscriptions do not include Tom UAM's administration — only once Tom SQM sends their invitations; until then every tenant of an installation is created by a platform administrator with its first top-level administrator (C1.4), and the operations Tom SQM calls are shipped and tested with the test client (BQ-424);
- keep the platform tenant out of suspension and deletion;
- create every tenant in one region of the installation, chosen at its creation within the regions its platform subscription offers, and name the region in the list of tenants (FR-97);
- show a new tenant's top-level administrators which setup steps —
  features, policies, organizations, applications, branding,
  administrators — are done and which are open, mark a step done when its
  condition holds in the tenant, and let each step be skipped; a
  one-person tenant counts as set up once its first application is
  enabled;
- guide a new tenant's top-level administrators through the setup as a wizard (DQ-139 (a)): besides the steps above, a step for each security-relevant setting — second factors and sessions, four-eyes and self-approval, break-glass, the tenant's own key with the key-recovery one-time passwords and the emergency-key setting `keys.emergencyKeyAllowed` (off by default, BQ-601 (a)), the retention periods, and tenant discovery `signIn.tenantDiscovery` (off by default, DQ-130 (b)); each step is a page that explains what the choice protects and what it gives up, preselects the recommended value, and saves it through the operation that sets it elsewhere, with that operation's step-up and four-eyes; a step can be skipped and taken up again (`setup.skippedSteps`), the setup overview shows the state of every step, and a top-level administrator reopens the wizard from `SETTINGS` at any time. The wizard opens by itself once, at the first top-level administrator's first sign-in to the opened tenant, with the settings the tenant's creation chose shown as done (DQ-141 (a)); afterwards the setup overview and `SETTINGS` reopen it. No step must be done before the tenant goes live: the defaults are the recommended values, and the setup overview keeps showing the open steps until each is done or skipped (DQ-142 (a)). The steps set what the requirements that own each setting ask: break-glass FRE-REQU-BREAK-GLASS, tenant discovery FRE-REQU-TENANT-REACH, four-eyes FRE-REQU-FOUR-EYES, second factors FRE-REQU-SECOND-FACTORS, sessions FRE-REQU-SESSIONS-SSO, the retention periods FRE-REQU-SETTINGS-HIERARCHY, the tenant's own key and the key-recovery passwords SECRQ-REQU-KEY-MANAGEMENT.

FRE-REQU-TENANT-OFFBOARDING refines deletion, the final export and the end
of the restore window.

RSP/functionalRequirements/FRE-REQU-LST-.description:
The system shall let the platform set a tenant's available
features at creation and change them later, and let the
tenant's administrators decide which available features are
enabled.

The per-tenant feature flags are:
- self-registration
- delegation
- onward delegation
- vacation presets
- emergency delegation
- four-eyes
- break-glass
- access reviews
- social login
- LDAP
- passwordless
- SCIM
- item sharing (FR-74)

It shall also:
- refuse an operation of a feature the platform has not made available or
  the tenant has not enabled with `UAM-403-FEATURE-DISABLED`, and not
  offer it in the client;
- show governance screens in the client only where their feature is
  enabled or work waits for the user;
- notify the tenant's top-level administrators when the platform changes
  the tenant's available features;
- on withdrawing an available feature the tenant has enabled, notify the tenant's top-level administrators and disable it in the tenant at a date after a notice period — 30 days by default, an installation setting; a withdrawal may set a later date, and an earlier one only for a security reason, recorded in the platform audit and named in the notice (BQ-404), keeping its data;
- let platform administrators switch an inbound sign-in protocol — OIDC,
  SAML, LDAP or social sign-in — off for every tenant at once as an
  emergency measure, and on again; switching needs two platform
  administrators — in an installation with one, that one as his own second under the platform tenant's self-approval setting, recorded as self-approval (FR-60, D-306, BQ-474) — and step-up, is recorded in the platform trail and in
  each affected tenant's trail, and is notified to the affected tenants'
  top-level administrators with the reason the switch names; switching off keeps every source's configuration, and switching on again restores sign-in through the sources unchanged.

expect.markdown: # Requirements Specification ## Functional Requirements [Also in [SBP FR](links.sbp.tomspecs.md#FR), held here]{.linked} ### Requirements #### FR-01 — Platform tenant and tenant lifecycle [Also in [SBP FRE-REQU-TENANT-LIFECYCLE](links.sbp.tomspecs.md#FRE-REQU-TENANT-LIFECYCLE), held here]{.linked} _Extrapolated — see iterations/sbpa21_notes.md._ | TomSpecField | Value | | --- | --- | | Status | approved | ##### Details | TomSpecField | Value | | --- | --- | | RequirementType | Workflow | | Category | Platform and tenancy | Description: The system shall run an installation as a reserved platform tenant plus customer tenants. - Platform administrators are users of the platform tenant holding scoped platform rights, and delegation, four-eyes and audit apply to them unchanged. - A tenant is in exactly one of the states provisioning, active, suspended or deleted. - Creating a tenant requires its first top-level administrator, and a second one when the four-eyes principle is enabled for the tenant, unless the first is to approve as his own second (self-approval, D-306). - The first administrator is invited by e-mail with a time-limited link to set a password and enrol a second factor. - Platform administrators delete a tenant with four-eyes; a deleted tenant stays restorable for 90 days, then follows its own pseudonymization and purge rules, and a final data export is offered. It shall also: - create a tenant in state provisioning with its slug, display name, available features, four-eyes choice — on unless switched off — and self-approval setting, refusing a slug that is used or reserved (D-306); - open the tenant (provisioning to active) once its first top-level administrator — both of them under four-eyes — has accepted the invitation; - let platform administrators delete a tenant still in provisioning whose administrators never accepted, revoking its pending invitations; - list the installation's tenants with slug, display name and state to platform administrators, without tenant data; - let Tom SQM create a tenant when a customer makes its first subscription — through an operation of the administration API, called with the platform tenant's service account for Tom SQM — with the customer's subscriptions bound to it from the start and the person whose address the customer gave during the subscription for the first administrator — by default the person subscribing — invited as its first top-level administrator where those subscriptions include Tom UAM's administration, otherwise as its first inviter (BQ-398); every tenant is bound by the subscriptions of its customer; - offer self-service tenants — tenants whose subscriptions do not include Tom UAM's administration — only once Tom SQM sends their invitations; until then every tenant of an installation is created by a platform administrator with its first top-level administrator (C1.4), and the operations Tom SQM calls are shipped and tested with the test client (BQ-424); - keep the platform tenant out of suspension and deletion; - create every tenant in one region of the installation, chosen at its creation within the regions its platform subscription offers, and name the region in the list of tenants (FR-97); - show a new tenant's top-level administrators which setup steps — features, policies, organizations, applications, branding, administrators — are done and which are open, mark a step done when its condition holds in the tenant, and let each step be skipped; a one-person tenant counts as set up once its first application is enabled; - guide a new tenant's top-level administrators through the setup as a wizard (DQ-139 (a)): besides the steps above, a step for each security-relevant setting — second factors and sessions, four-eyes and self-approval, break-glass, the tenant's own key with the key-recovery one-time passwords and the emergency-key setting `keys.emergencyKeyAllowed` (off by default, BQ-601 (a)), the retention periods, and tenant discovery `signIn.tenantDiscovery` (off by default, DQ-130 (b)); each step is a page that explains what the choice protects and what it gives up, preselects the recommended value, and saves it through the operation that sets it elsewhere, with that operation's step-up and four-eyes; a step can be skipped and taken up again (`setup.skippedSteps`), the setup overview shows the state of every step, and a top-level administrator reopens the wizard from `SETTINGS` at any time. The wizard opens by itself once, at the first top-level administrator's first sign-in to the opened tenant, with the settings the tenant's creation chose shown as done (DQ-141 (a)); afterwards the setup overview and `SETTINGS` reopen it. No step must be done before the tenant goes live: the defaults are the recommended values, and the setup overview keeps showing the open steps until each is done or skipped (DQ-142 (a)). The steps set what the requirements that own each setting ask: break-glass FRE-REQU-BREAK-GLASS, tenant discovery FRE-REQU-TENANT-REACH, four-eyes FRE-REQU-FOUR-EYES, second factors FRE-REQU-SECOND-FACTORS, sessions FRE-REQU-SESSIONS-SSO, the retention periods FRE-REQU-SETTINGS-HIERARCHY, the tenant's own key and the key-recovery passwords SECRQ-REQU-KEY-MANAGEMENT. FRE-REQU-TENANT-OFFBOARDING refines deletion, the final export and the end of the restore window. ##### Priority | TomSpecField | Value | | --- | --- | | Priority | must | | BusinessValue | critical | ##### Source | TomSpecField | Value | | --- | --- | | RequestDate | 2026-10-11 — the product owner's statement and the answers of question rounds 1–3 of the Project Idea (section 11, *Decision log*), which its source cites; SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.description:
The system shall run an installation as a reserved platform
tenant plus customer tenants.
- Platform administrators are users of the platform tenant
  holding scoped platform rights, and delegation, four-eyes
  and audit apply to them unchanged.
- A tenant is in exactly one of the states provisioning,
  active, suspended or deleted.
- Creating a tenant requires its first top-level
  administrator, and a second one when the four-eyes principle
  is enabled for the tenant, unless the first is to approve as
  his own second (self-approval, D-306).
- The first administrator is invited by e-mail with a
  time-limited link to set a password and enrol a second
  factor.
- Platform administrators delete a tenant with four-eyes; a
  deleted tenant stays restorable for 90 days, then follows
  its own pseudonymization and purge rules, and a final data
  export is offered.

It shall also:
- create a tenant in state provisioning with its slug, display name,
  available features, four-eyes choice — on unless switched off — and
  self-approval setting, refusing a slug that is used or reserved
  (D-306);
- open the tenant (provisioning to active) once its first top-level
  administrator — both of them under four-eyes — has accepted the
  invitation;
- let platform administrators delete a tenant still in provisioning whose
  administrators never accepted, revoking its pending invitations;
- list the installation's tenants with slug, display name and state to
  platform administrators, without tenant data;
- let Tom SQM create a tenant when a customer makes its first subscription — through an operation of the administration API, called with the platform tenant's service account for Tom SQM — with the customer's subscriptions bound to it from the start and the person whose address the customer gave during the subscription for the first administrator — by default the person subscribing — invited as its first top-level administrator where those subscriptions include Tom UAM's administration, otherwise as its first inviter (BQ-398); every tenant is bound by the subscriptions of its customer;
- offer self-service tenants — tenants whose subscriptions do not include Tom UAM's administration — only once Tom SQM sends their invitations; until then every tenant of an installation is created by a platform administrator with its first top-level administrator (C1.4), and the operations Tom SQM calls are shipped and tested with the test client (BQ-424);
- keep the platform tenant out of suspension and deletion;
- create every tenant in one region of the installation, chosen at its creation within the regions its platform subscription offers, and name the region in the list of tenants (FR-97);
- show a new tenant's top-level administrators which setup steps —
  features, policies, organizations, applications, branding,
  administrators — are done and which are open, mark a step done when its
  condition holds in the tenant, and let each step be skipped; a
  one-person tenant counts as set up once its first application is
  enabled;
- guide a new tenant's top-level administrators through the setup as a wizard (DQ-139 (a)): besides the steps above, a step for each security-relevant setting — second factors and sessions, four-eyes and self-approval, break-glass, the tenant's own key with the key-recovery one-time passwords and the emergency-key setting `keys.emergencyKeyAllowed` (off by default, BQ-601 (a)), the retention periods, and tenant discovery `signIn.tenantDiscovery` (off by default, DQ-130 (b)); each step is a page that explains what the choice protects and what it gives up, preselects the recommended value, and saves it through the operation that sets it elsewhere, with that operation's step-up and four-eyes; a step can be skipped and taken up again (`setup.skippedSteps`), the setup overview shows the state of every step, and a top-level administrator reopens the wizard from `SETTINGS` at any time. The wizard opens by itself once, at the first top-level administrator's first sign-in to the opened tenant, with the settings the tenant's creation chose shown as done (DQ-141 (a)); afterwards the setup overview and `SETTINGS` reopen it. No step must be done before the tenant goes live: the defaults are the recommended values, and the setup overview keeps showing the open steps until each is done or skipped (DQ-142 (a)). The steps set what the requirements that own each setting ask: break-glass FRE-REQU-BREAK-GLASS, tenant discovery FRE-REQU-TENANT-REACH, four-eyes FRE-REQU-FOUR-EYES, second factors FRE-REQU-SECOND-FACTORS, sessions FRE-REQU-SESSIONS-SSO, the retention periods FRE-REQU-SETTINGS-HIERARCHY, the tenant's own key and the key-recovery passwords SECRQ-REQU-KEY-MANAGEMENT.

FRE-REQU-TENANT-OFFBOARDING refines deletion, the final export and the end
of the restore window.

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.fitCriterion: Met when all 13 acceptance criteria of the requirement pass (`RAC > ACE-CRIT-LST`, ACE-CRIT-1 … ACE-CRIT-13)

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A platform administrator creating a tenant with the four-eyes principle enabled
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The tenant is not created and the request is refused as incomplete; with the setting on it is created
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: The creation request names only one top-level administrator and leaves the self-approval setting off

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: An installation with two customer tenants, one in region `eu-1` and one in `ch-1`
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: Each row shows slug, display name, state and region, and nothing from inside the tenants
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: A platform administrator lists the installation's tenants

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A new tenant whose top-level administrator opens the setup wizard
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The page has explained what discovery opens and what it keeps closed, the recommended value — off — was preselected and is saved through the settings operation, and the step counts as done (DQ-139 (a), DQ-130 (b))
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: The administrator reaches the step of tenant discovery and goes on without changing it

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A tenant whose top-level administrator skipped the step of the tenant's own key in the setup wizard
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The wizard offers the skipped step again; setting the key there asks the step-up and, with four-eyes on, holds the change for a second top-level administrator, as on `SETTINGS` (DQ-139 (a), SR-06)
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: A top-level administrator reopens the wizard from `SETTINGS`

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A tenant just opened, created with four-eyes on, whose first top-level administrator has not signed in yet
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The setup wizard opens by itself, the four-eyes step shown as done; leaving it without saving any step keeps the tenant active with the default values, and at the next sign-in the setup overview shows the open steps instead of the wizard (DQ-141 (a), DQ-142 (a))
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: That administrator signs in for the first time

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A tenant deleted by platform administrators with four-eyes approval
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The tenant returns with its data; after 90 days it follows its own pseudonymization and purge rules instead
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: Platform administrators restore it within 90 days of the deletion

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A slug held by an existing tenant or left by a purged one
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The request is refused with `UAM-409-CONFLICT` and no tenant is created
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: A platform administrator creates a tenant with that slug

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A tenant in provisioning with four-eyes on and two invited top-level administrators
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The tenant stays in provisioning; it becomes active and shows the setup overview when the second accepts
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: Only the first of them accepts the invitation

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A new tenant whose only user is its top-level administrator
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The setup overview counts the tenant as set up; the remaining steps stay offered and can be skipped
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: The administrator enables the tenant's first application

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A customer making its first platform subscription through Tom SQM, the subscription including Tom UAM's administration and naming an administrator's e-mail address
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: A tenant in provisioning is created with the customer's platform subscriptions bound to it, the named address is invited as its first top-level administrator, and the tenant becomes active when the invitation is accepted
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: Tom SQM calls the tenant-creation operation with the platform tenant's service account

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A first platform subscription that does not include Tom UAM's administration and names no administrator's address
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The person subscribing is invited as the tenant's first inviter, holds no administrative right, and the tenant runs on its levels' presets in self-service
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: Tom SQM creates the tenant — or, until Tom SQM exists, the test client calls the same operation (BQ-424)

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: The platform tenant of an installation and a customer tenant
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: Both requests are refused and the platform tenant stays active; the customer tenant can still be suspended and deleted
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: Two platform administrators try to suspend the platform tenant, and later to delete it

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.given: A tenant in provisioning whose first top-level administrator has not accepted the invitation
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.then: The tenant is deleted, its pending invitations are revoked so that the invitation link no longer works, and the deletion is recorded in the platform audit
SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.when: A platform administrator deletes the tenant

SBP/introductionAndScope/requirements/fu.description:
The system shall let the platform set a tenant's available
features at creation and change them later, and let the
tenant's administrators decide which available features are
enabled.

The per-tenant feature flags are:
- self-registration
- delegation
- onward delegation
- vacation presets
- emergency delegation
- four-eyes
- break-glass
- access reviews
- social login
- LDAP
- passwordless
- SCIM
- item sharing (FR-74)

It shall also:
- refuse an operation of a feature the platform has not made available or
  the tenant has not enabled with `UAM-403-FEATURE-DISABLED`, and not
  offer it in the client;
- show governance screens in the client only where their feature is
  enabled or work waits for the user;
- notify the tenant's top-level administrators when the platform changes
  the tenant's available features;
- on withdrawing an available feature the tenant has enabled, notify the tenant's top-level administrators and disable it in the tenant at a date after a notice period — 30 days by default, an installation setting; a withdrawal may set a later date, and an earlier one only for a security reason, recorded in the platform audit and named in the notice (BQ-404), keeping its data;
- let platform administrators switch an inbound sign-in protocol — OIDC,
  SAML, LDAP or social sign-in — off for every tenant at once as an
  emergency measure, and on again; switching needs two platform
  administrators — in an installation with one, that one as his own second under the platform tenant's self-approval setting, recorded as self-approval (FR-60, D-306, BQ-474) — and step-up, is recorded in the platform trail and in
  each affected tenant's trail, and is notified to the affected tenants'
  top-level administrators with the reason the switch names; switching off keeps every source's configuration, and switching on again restores sign-in through the sources unchanged.

What a tenant may use is the platform's decision and what it uses is the
tenant's; keeping the two apart lets subscriptions bound a tenant without the
platform switching the tenant's features for it (C1.6, C14.2).

until then every tenant of an installation is created by a platform administrator with its first top-level administrator (C1.4), and the operations Tom SQM calls are shipped and tested with the test client (BQ-424); - keep the platform tenant out of suspension and deletion; - create every tenant in one region of the installation, chosen at its creation within the regions its platform subscription offers, and name the region in the list of tenants (FR-97); - show a new tenant's top-level administrators which setup steps — features, policies, organizations, applications, branding, administrators — are done and which are open, mark a step done when its condition holds in the tenant, and let each step be skipped; a one-person tenant counts as set up once its first application is enabled; - guide a new tenant's top-level administrators through the setup as a wizard (DQ-139 (a)): besides the steps above, a step for each security-relevant setting — second factors and sessions, four-eyes and self-approval, break-glass, the tenant's own key with the key-recovery one-time passwords and the emergency-key setting `keys.emergencyKeyAllowed` (off by default, BQ-601 (a)), the retention periods, and tenant discovery `signIn.tenantDiscovery` (off by default, DQ-130 (b)); No step must be done before the tenant goes live: the defaults are the recommended values, and the setup overview keeps showing the open steps until each is done or skipped (DQ-142 (a)). RSP/functionalRequirements/FRE-REQU-LST-.description:
The system shall run an installation as a reserved platform
tenant plus customer tenants.
- Platform administrators are users of the platform tenant
  holding scoped platform rights, and delegation, four-eyes
  and audit apply to them unchanged.
- A tenant is in exactly one of the states provisioning,
  active, suspended or deleted.
- Creating a tenant requires its first top-level
  administrator, and a second one when the four-eyes principle
  is enabled for the tenant, unless the first is to approve as
  his own second (self-approval, D-306).
- The first administrator is invited by e-mail with a
  time-limited link to set a password and enrol a second
  factor.
- Platform administrators delete a tenant with four-eyes; a
  deleted tenant stays restorable for 90 days, then follows
  its own pseudonymization and purge rules, and a final data
  export is offered.

It shall also:
- create a tenant in state provisioning with its slug, display name,
  available features, four-eyes choice — on unless switched off — and
  self-approval setting, refusing a slug that is used or reserved
  (D-306);
- open the tenant (provisioning to active) once its first top-level
  administrator — both of them under four-eyes — has accepted the
  invitation;
- let platform administrators delete a tenant still in provisioning whose
  administrators never accepted, revoking its pending invitations;
- list the installation's tenants with slug, display name and state to
  platform administrators, without tenant data;
- let Tom SQM create a tenant when a customer makes its first subscription — through an operation of the administration API, called with the platform tenant's service account for Tom SQM — with the customer's subscriptions bound to it from the start and the person whose address the customer gave during the subscription for the first administrator — by default the person subscribing — invited as its first top-level administrator where those subscriptions include Tom UAM's administration, otherwise as its first inviter (BQ-398); every tenant is bound by the subscriptions of its customer;
- offer self-service tenants — tenants whose subscriptions do not include Tom UAM's administration — only once Tom SQM sends their invitations; until then every tenant of an installation is created by a platform administrator with its first top-level administrator (C1.4), and the operations Tom SQM calls are shipped and tested with the test client (BQ-424);
- keep the platform tenant out of suspension and deletion;
- create every tenant in one region of the installation, chosen at its creation within the regions its platform subscription offers, and name the region in the list of tenants (FR-97);
- show a new tenant's top-level administrators which setup steps —
  features, policies, organizations, applications, branding,
  administrators — are done and which are open, mark a step done when its
  condition holds in the tenant, and let each step be skipped; a
  one-person tenant counts as set up once its first application is
  enabled;
- guide a new tenant's top-level administrators through the setup as a wizard (DQ-139 (a)): besides the steps above, a step for each security-relevant setting — second factors and sessions, four-eyes and self-approval, break-glass, the tenant's own key with the key-recovery one-time passwords and the emergency-key setting `keys.emergencyKeyAllowed` (off by default, BQ-601 (a)), the retention periods, and tenant discovery `signIn.tenantDiscovery` (off by default, DQ-130 (b)); each step is a page that explains what the choice protects and what it gives up, preselects the recommended value, and saves it through the operation that sets it elsewhere, with that operation's step-up and four-eyes; a step can be skipped and taken up again (`setup.skippedSteps`), the setup overview shows the state of every step, and a top-level administrator reopens the wizard from `SETTINGS` at any time. The wizard opens by itself once, at the first top-level administrator's first sign-in to the opened tenant, with the settings the tenant's creation chose shown as done (DQ-141 (a)); afterwards the setup overview and `SETTINGS` reopen it. No step must be done before the tenant goes live: the defaults are the recommended values, and the setup overview keeps showing the open steps until each is done or skipped (DQ-142 (a)). The steps set what the requirements that own each setting ask: break-glass FRE-REQU-BREAK-GLASS, tenant discovery FRE-REQU-TENANT-REACH, four-eyes FRE-REQU-FOUR-EYES, second factors FRE-REQU-SECOND-FACTORS, sessions FRE-REQU-SESSIONS-SSO, the retention periods FRE-REQU-SETTINGS-HIERARCHY, the tenant's own key and the key-recovery passwords SECRQ-REQU-KEY-MANAGEMENT.

FRE-REQU-TENANT-OFFBOARDING refines deletion, the final export and the end
of the restore window.

RSP/functionalRequirements/FRE-REQU-LST-.description:
The system shall let the platform set a tenant's available
features at creation and change them later, and let the
tenant's administrators decide which available features are
enabled.

The per-tenant feature flags are:
- self-registration
- delegation
- onward delegation
- vacation presets
- emergency delegation
- four-eyes
- break-glass
- access reviews
- social login
- LDAP
- passwordless
- SCIM
- item sharing (FR-74)

It shall also:
- refuse an operation of a feature the platform has not made available or
  the tenant has not enabled with `UAM-403-FEATURE-DISABLED`, and not
  offer it in the client;
- show governance screens in the client only where their feature is
  enabled or work waits for the user;
- notify the tenant's top-level administrators when the platform changes
  the tenant's available features;
- on withdrawing an available feature the tenant has enabled, notify the tenant's top-level administrators and disable it in the tenant at a date after a notice period — 30 days by default, an installation setting; a withdrawal may set a later date, and an earlier one only for a security reason, recorded in the platform audit and named in the notice (BQ-404), keeping its data;
- let platform administrators switch an inbound sign-in protocol — OIDC,
  SAML, LDAP or social sign-in — off for every tenant at once as an
  emergency measure, and on again; switching needs two platform
  administrators — in an installation with one, that one as his own second under the platform tenant's self-approval setting, recorded as self-approval (FR-60, D-306, BQ-474) — and step-up, is recorded in the platform trail and in
  each affected tenant's trail, and is notified to the affected tenants'
  top-level administrators with the reason the switch names; switching off keeps every source's configuration, and switching on again restores sign-in through the sources unchanged.

The per-tenant feature flags are: - self-registration - delegation - onward delegation - vacation presets - emergency delegation - four-eyes - break-glass - access reviews - social login - LDAP - passwordless - SCIM - item sharing (FR-74) It shall also: - refuse an operation of a feature the platform has not made available or the tenant has not enabled with `UAM-403-FEATURE-DISABLED`, and not offer it in the client; - show governance screens in the client only where their feature is enabled or work waits for the user; - notify the tenant's top-level administrators when the platform changes the tenant's available features; - on withdrawing an available feature the tenant has enabled, notify the tenant's top-level administrators and disable it in the tenant at a date after a notice period — 30 days by default, an installation setting; a withdrawal may set a later date, and an earlier one only for a security reason, recorded in the platform audit and named in the notice (BQ-404), keeping its data; - let platform administrators switch an inbound sign-in protocol — OIDC, SAML, LDAP or social sign-in — off for every tenant at once as an emergency measure, and on again; switching needs two platform administrators — in an installation with one, that one as his own second under the platform tenant's self-approval setting, recorded as self-approval (FR-60, D-306, BQ-474) — and step-up, is recorded in the platform trail and in each affected tenant's trail, and is notified to the affected tenants' top-level administrators with the reason the switch names; expect.given: # Requirements Specification ## Functional Requirements [Also in [SBP FR](links.sbp.tomspecs.md#FR), held here]{.linked} ### Requirements #### FR-01 — Platform tenant and tenant lifecycle [Also in [SBP FRE-REQU-TENANT-LIFECYCLE](links.sbp.tomspecs.md#FRE-REQU-TENANT-LIFECYCLE), held here]{.linked} _Extrapolated — see iterations/sbpa21_notes.md._ | TomSpecField | Value | | --- | --- | | Status | approved | ##### Details | TomSpecField | Value | | --- | --- | | RequirementType | Workflow | | Category | Platform and tenancy | Description: The system shall run an installation as a reserved platform tenant plus customer tenants. - Platform administrators are users of the platform tenant holding scoped platform rights, and delegation, four-eyes and audit apply to them unchanged. - A tenant is in exactly one of the states provisioning, active, suspended or deleted. - Creating a tenant requires its first top-level administrator, and a second one when the four-eyes principle is enabled for the tenant, unless the first is to approve as his own second (self-approval, D-306). - The first administrator is invited by e-mail with a time-limited link to set a password and enrol a second factor. - Platform administrators delete a tenant with four-eyes; a deleted tenant stays restorable for 90 days, then follows its own pseudonymization and purge rules, and a final data export is offered. It shall also: - create a tenant in state provisioning with its slug, display name, available features, four-eyes choice — on unless switched off — and self-approval setting, refusing a slug that is used or reserved (D-306); - open the tenant (provisioning to active) once its first top-level administrator — both of them under four-eyes — has accepted the invitation; - let platform administrators delete a tenant still in provisioning whose administrators never accepted, revoking its pending invitations; - list the installation's tenants with slug, display name and state to platform administrators, without tenant data; - let Tom SQM create a tenant when a customer makes its first subscription — through an operation of the administration API, called with the platform tenant's service account for Tom SQM — with the customer's subscriptions bound to it from the start and the person whose address the customer gave during the subscription for the first administrator — by default the person subscribing — invited as its first top-level administrator where those subscriptions include Tom UAM's administration, otherwise as its first inviter (BQ-398); every tenant is bound by the subscriptions of its customer; - offer self-service tenants — tenants whose subscriptions do not include Tom UAM's administration — only once Tom SQM sends their invitations; until then every tenant of an installation is created by a platform administrator with its first top-level administrator (C1.4), and the operations Tom SQM calls are shipped and tested with the test client (BQ-424); - keep the platform tenant out of suspension and deletion; - create every tenant in one region of the installation, chosen at its creation within the regions its platform subscription offers, and name the region in the list of tenants (FR-97); - show a new tenant's top-level administrators which setup steps — features, policies, organizations, applications, branding, administrators — are done and which are open, mark a step done when its condition holds in the tenant, and let each step be skipped; a one-person tenant counts as set up once its first application is enabled; - guide a new tenant's top-level administrators through the setup as a wizard (DQ-139 (a)): besides the steps above, a step for each security-relevant setting — second factors and sessions, four-eyes and self-approval, break-glass, the tenant's own key with the key-recovery one-time passwords and the emergency-key setting `keys.emergencyKeyAllowed` (off by default, BQ-601 (a)), the retention periods, and tenant discovery `signIn.tenantDiscovery` (off by default, DQ-130 (b)); each step is a page that explains what the choice protects and what it gives up, preselects the recommended value, and saves it through the operation that sets it elsewhere, with that operation's step-up and four-eyes; a step can be skipped and taken up again (`setup.skippedSteps`), the setup overview shows the state of every step, and a top-level administrator reopens the wizard from `SETTINGS` at any time. The wizard opens by itself once, at the first top-level administrator's first sign-in to the opened tenant, with the settings the tenant's creation chose shown as done (DQ-141 (a)); afterwards the setup overview and `SETTINGS` reopen it. No step must be done before the tenant goes live: the defaults are the recommended values, and the setup overview keeps showing the open steps until each is done or skipped (DQ-142 (a)). The steps set what the requirements that own each setting ask: break-glass FRE-REQU-BREAK-GLASS, tenant discovery FRE-REQU-TENANT-REACH, four-eyes FRE-REQU-FOUR-EYES, second factors FRE-REQU-SECOND-FACTORS, sessions FRE-REQU-SESSIONS-SSO, the retention periods FRE-REQU-SETTINGS-HIERARCHY, the tenant's own key and the key-recovery passwords SECRQ-REQU-KEY-MANAGEMENT. RSP/functionalRequirements/FRE-REQU-LST-.description:
The system shall run an installation as a reserved platform
tenant plus customer tenants.
- Platform administrators are users of the platform tenant
  holding scoped platform rights, and delegation, four-eyes
  and audit apply to them unchanged.
- A tenant is in exactly one of the states provisioning,
  active, suspended or deleted.
- Creating a tenant requires its first top-level
  administrator, and a second one when the four-eyes principle
  is enabled for the tenant, unless the first is to approve as
  his own second (self-approval, D-306).
- The first administrator is invited by e-mail with a
  time-limited link to set a password and enrol a second
  factor.
- Platform administrators delete a tenant with four-eyes; a
  deleted tenant stays restorable for 90 days, then follows
  its own pseudonymization and purge rules, and a final data
  export is offered.

It shall also:
- create a tenant in state provisioning with its slug, display name,
  available features, four-eyes choice — on unless switched off — and
  self-approval setting, refusing a slug that is used or reserved
  (D-306);
- open the tenant (provisioning to active) once its first top-level
  administrator — both of them under four-eyes — has accepted the
  invitation;
- let platform administrators delete a tenant still in provisioning whose
  administrators never accepted, revoking its pending invitations;
- list the installation's tenants with slug, display name and state to
  platform administrators, without tenant data;
- let Tom SQM create a tenant when a customer makes its first subscription — through an operation of the administration API, called with the platform tenant's service account for Tom SQM — with the customer's subscriptions bound to it from the start and the person whose address the customer gave during the subscription for the first administrator — by default the person subscribing — invited as its first top-level administrator where those subscriptions include Tom UAM's administration, otherwise as its first inviter (BQ-398); every tenant is bound by the subscriptions of its customer;
- offer self-service tenants — tenants whose subscriptions do not include Tom UAM's administration — only once Tom SQM sends their invitations; until then every tenant of an installation is created by a platform administrator with its first top-level administrator (C1.4), and the operations Tom SQM calls are shipped and tested with the test client (BQ-424);
- keep the platform tenant out of suspension and deletion;
- create every tenant in one region of the installation, chosen at its creation within the regions its platform subscription offers, and name the region in the list of tenants (FR-97);
- show a new tenant's top-level administrators which setup steps —
  features, policies, organizations, applications, branding,
  administrators — are done and which are open, mark a step done when its
  condition holds in the tenant, and let each step be skipped; a
  one-person tenant counts as set up once its first application is
  enabled;
- guide a new tenant's top-level administrators through the setup as a wizard (DQ-139 (a)): besides the steps above, a step for each security-relevant setting — second factors and sessions, four-eyes and self-approval, break-glass, the tenant's own key with the key-recovery one-time passwords and the emergency-key setting `keys.emergencyKeyAllowed` (off by default, BQ-601 (a)), the retention periods, and tenant discovery `signIn.tenantDiscovery` (off by default, DQ-130 (b)); each step is a page that explains what the choice protects and what it gives up, preselects the recommended value, and saves it through the operation that sets it elsewhere, with that operation's step-up and four-eyes; a step can be skipped and taken up again (`setup.skippedSteps`), the setup overview shows the state of every step, and a top-level administrator reopens the wizard from `SETTINGS` at any time. The wizard opens by itself once, at the first top-level administrator's first sign-in to the opened tenant, with the settings the tenant's creation chose shown as done (DQ-141 (a)); afterwards the setup overview and `SETTINGS` reopen it. No step must be done before the tenant goes live: the defaults are the recommended values, and the setup overview keeps showing the open steps until each is done or skipped (DQ-142 (a)). The steps set what the requirements that own each setting ask: break-glass FRE-REQU-BREAK-GLASS, tenant discovery FRE-REQU-TENANT-REACH, four-eyes FRE-REQU-FOUR-EYES, second factors FRE-REQU-SECOND-FACTORS, sessions FRE-REQU-SESSIONS-SSO, the retention periods FRE-REQU-SETTINGS-HIERARCHY, the tenant's own key and the key-recovery passwords SECRQ-REQU-KEY-MANAGEMENT.

FRE-REQU-TENANT-OFFBOARDING refines deletion, the final export and the end
of the restore window.

RSP/functionalRequirements/FRE-REQU-LST-.description:
The system shall let the platform set a tenant's available
features at creation and change them later, and let the
tenant's administrators decide which available features are
enabled.

The per-tenant feature flags are:
- self-registration
- delegation
- onward delegation
- vacation presets
- emergency delegation
- four-eyes
- break-glass
- access reviews
- social login
- LDAP
- passwordless
- SCIM
- item sharing (FR-74)

It shall also:
- refuse an operation of a feature the platform has not made available or
  the tenant has not enabled with `UAM-403-FEATURE-DISABLED`, and not
  offer it in the client;
- show governance screens in the client only where their feature is
  enabled or work waits for the user;
- notify the tenant's top-level administrators when the platform changes
  the tenant's available features;
- on withdrawing an available feature the tenant has enabled, notify the tenant's top-level administrators and disable it in the tenant at a date after a notice period — 30 days by default, an installation setting; a withdrawal may set a later date, and an earlier one only for a security reason, recorded in the platform audit and named in the notice (BQ-404), keeping its data;
- let platform administrators switch an inbound sign-in protocol — OIDC,
  SAML, LDAP or social sign-in — off for every tenant at once as an
  emergency measure, and on again; switching needs two platform
  administrators — in an installation with one, that one as his own second under the platform tenant's self-approval setting, recorded as self-approval (FR-60, D-306, BQ-474) — and step-up, is recorded in the platform trail and in
  each affected tenant's trail, and is notified to the affected tenants'
  top-level administrators with the reason the switch names; switching off keeps every source's configuration, and switching on again restores sign-in through the sources unchanged.
